Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

what pronoun and adjective

what? (a question)

also what is it?, what’s that?, what is this?, what (that which)

classical

Ter. And. 139: Quid fēcī?
Cic. Att. 7.11.1: quaesō, quid est hoc?

quid

neuter of the interrogative pronoun quis

what?

With a genitive it asks how much of a thing: quid novī?, what news?; quid cēnae?, what is there for dinner? (Ter. Haut. 211). Quid? alone also asks why: see “why”.

Other words

  • quī, quae, quod — what … ? (with a noun)

    interrogative adjective · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.5: quō cibō

    See “which” (question).

  • id quod (quod) — what (that which)

    relative · also used · classical · Publ. Q 80: Quod quisque amat, laudandō commendat sibi.

    The “what” of a statement, “I like what you made”: id quod, or quod alone when its clause comes first.

Examples

  • Quid fēcī? quid commeruī aut peccāvī, pater?

    What have I done? What have I deserved, Father, or what wrong have I done?Ter. And. 139

  • Quid ais? quid nōmen tibi est?

    What’s that? What’s your name?Plaut. Amph. 364b

  • quaesō, quid est hoc? aut quid agitur? mihi enim tenebrae sunt

    tell me, what is this? What is going on? I am in the darkCic. Att. 7.11.1

  • tamen quid habuistis in cēnā?

    so what did you have at dinner?Petr. 66.1

  • Quod quisque amat, laudandō commendat sibi.

    What each of us loves, we make dearer to ourselves by praising it.Publ. Q 80

See also which, what kind of, whatever, why, what happened?, what do you want?.
